stage_notes:
RE-RUN OF STAGE 4 AGAINST REAL COUNTS. The prior stage-4 pass used a dataset_schema.json whose subgroup sizes were formula-derived (cohort-wide prevalence percentages multiplied into aggregate totals). That schema has been replaced with counts computed directly from data_mutations.txt (208,544 rows, 23,867 sequenced samples) and data_timeline_treatment.txt (134,943 administration rows). Every number below is recomputed from the new file; no figure is carried over from the prior run. Method is unchanged so the two runs are comparable: variance of a log contrast = sum of inverse event counts over the identifying cells, events = patients x an assumed event fraction f, minimum detectable effect at alpha 0.05 / 80% power = exp(2.802 x SE), reported at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8 with f = 0.6 as reference, plus an explicit adequacy judgement against the effect size the literature reports.

OUTCOME: 3 pass (H-001, H-002, H-009), 4 reject on a missing required field (H-007, H-008, H-010 on PD-L1 TPS band; H-014 on allelic status), 2 underpowered (H-004, H-011). Prior run was 4 pass / 4 reject / 1 underpowered.

VERDICTS THAT CHANGED: exactly one. H-011 moves from PASS to UNDERPOWERED. The prior run derived ~3,060 analysable ICI-treated NSCLC patients with ~430 STK11-mutants from a 5,680 cohort-wide ICI figure and an assumed 70% NSCLC share; the real numbers are 2,665 ICI-treated NSCLC patients with 336 STK11-LoF among them, i.e. the exposed cell is 22% smaller and the prevalence is 12.6% rather than the assumed 14.1%. The continuous TMB-by-STK11 interaction now detects a per-SD ratio-of-hazard-ratios of 1.26 at f = 0.6 (1.38 if TMB comparability forces restriction to the single dominant panel, IMPACT468, which the real by_gene_panel distribution shows is only 50.2% of NSCLC). The prior run judged that adequate on the reasoning that the mechanism implies an effect 'well beyond 1.25-fold'. That reasoning does not survive being written out: if the TMB slope in STK11-wildtype tumours is a per-SD HR of about 0.80-0.85, which is what within-ICI-arm TMB associations actually look like, then TOTAL abolition of the slope in STK11-mutants is a ratio of only 1.18-1.25 and sits below the detection threshold. The design can only detect abolition of an implausibly steep wild-type slope. That is the definition of inadequate, and passing it because the hypothesis is interesting is the failure mode this stage exists to prevent.

VERDICTS THAT STAYED THE SAME (but whose supporting arithmetic changed materially, in both directions):
- H-001 PASS, but the equivalence margin recommendation changes. See the block; this is the largest quantitative correction in the set.
- H-002 PASS. Gene-versus-gene detectable ratio worsens from 1.57 to 1.76 at f = 0.6, because the real STK11-KEAP1 co-mutation count (512 of 1,013 STK11-altered, i.e. 50.5% co-occurrence) is far higher than the 30% the prior run assumed, which shrinks both identifying single-mutant cells.
- H-004 UNDERPOWERED. See below; the raw cell correction was large and favourable and the verdict still does not move.
- H-007, H-008, H-010 REJECT on PD-L1. The basis is NARROWER than last time and needed re-examination. Last run said PD-L1 was absent from the schema entirely. That is no longer true: pdl1_sample_nlp (Yes 2143 / No 1176 / NA 4490) and pdl1_history_nlp (Yes 2988 / No 3241 / NA 1580) are real. But they are BINARY positive/negative flags from NLP, not a TPS percentage, and all three hypotheses are defined on TPS bands: H-007 stratifies within <1% / 1-49% / >=50%, H-008 IS the >=50% stratum, H-010 restricts to >=50% to defuse confounding by indication. A binary 'positive' pools 1-49% with >=50% and is exactly the distinction all three need. So the field is now present-but-wrong rather than absent, and the rejection stands on the same clause of the same statements. Two further points make it firmer, not softer: the binary flag is nlp_extracted, so it would be an NLP-derived PRIMARY stratifier rather than a covariate; and pdl1_sample_nlp is 57.5% NA, so even the binary version is missing for the majority. Note also a probable schema bug: neither pdl1 field is declared in the `tables` section at all, appearing only under cohort_counts.nsclc_detail, so no table/field name exists to put in a cohort spec.
- H-014 REJECT on allelic status. Nothing in the new schema touches this. There is still no LOH call, no allele-specific or total copy number at the locus, no cancer-cell-fraction/clonality field; alteration_type still offers a bare 'deletion' with no depth qualifier, so a deletion call cannot be assumed homozygous; tumor_purity is still nullable with no completeness figure published. The VAF-plus-purity derivation remains structurally unidentified (two unknowns, one observation) and is flagged, not engineered around. Secondary power got worse: the real first-line-ICI STK11-LoF pool gives ~50-90 patients per zygosity stratum, not the 90-120 the prior run derived.

THE TWO SPECIFICALLY FLAGGED ITEMS.
(1) H-004. The identifying cell never_smoker_egfr_alk_wt_stk11lof is 34, not the 8-10 the prior run estimated - a real fourfold correction in the hypothesis's favour. It does not rescue it, and the reason is instructive: 34 is the count in ALL NSCLC, with no treatment restriction, and the hypothesis is about first-line ICI-containing therapy. Only 46.9% of STK11-LoF patients received any anti-PD-1/PD-L1 agent (336/716, real), and of those roughly two thirds in first line, so the analysable cell is ~10 (first-line) to ~16 (any line) - essentially where the prior run's realistic scenario already put it. Minimum detectable smoking-by-STK11 ratio-of-hazard-ratios is 3.37 at f = 0.6 and 2.86 at f = 0.8, against a prior-run figure of 'above 3.2'. Even the absolute ceiling - dropping the ICI restriction entirely, which is a different hypothesis - only reaches 1.93. Nothing in the literature predicts a smoking-by-STK11 interaction of 1.9-fold, let alone 3-fold.
(2) H-001. The chemotherapy-arm STK11-LoF cell is 163, not the ~330 the prior run derived, and this cell alone now contributes 61% of the interaction variance. On the raw real cells (336 / 2329 / 163 / 1844) the minimum detectable ratio-of-hazard-ratios is 1.56 / 1.44 / 1.37 at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8, against the prior run's 1.47 / 1.37 / 1.31. After the first-line, stage and EGFR/ALK restrictions the hypothesis itself specifies it is 1.72 / 1.55 / 1.46. THE EQUIVALENCE MARGIN OF 1.4 THAT THE PRIOR RUN RECOMMENDED IS NO LONGER ACHIEVABLE. Bounding the interaction inside 1.4 with 80% power under the two-one-sided-tests convention requires SE(log ROR) <= 0.135, which on the analysable cells needs an event fraction of 0.72; under the stricter 95%-CI-inside-the-margin convention it needs 0.91. Neither is plausible. The margin must be prespecified at 1.5 (TOST) or 1.6 (95% CI). This is worse than the prior run, not better, and it is the one place where the formula-derived schema was actively flattering.

STATED ONCE: DERIVATION ASSUMPTIONS. The schema's by_treatment_exposure gives real NSCLC treatment counts but is not cross-tabulated with line of therapy, histology or driver status, so four multipliers are assumed rather than counted. (A1) EGFR/ALK/ROS1-activating driver exclusion removes ~15% of the ICI-treated NSCLC cohort and ~12% of the platinum-no-ICI cohort; EGFR/ALK patients are concentrated in the KRAS-wildtype and never-smoker strata, so where a cell is KRAS-wildtype the multiplier used is ~0.72 and this is stated in each block. (A2) 65% of ICI-exposed NSCLC received the agent in first line; MSK-CHORD spans both the second-line-monotherapy era and the first-line era. (A3) ICI monotherapy versus chemo-immunotherapy splits ~35/65 among first-line ICI recipients. (A4) The event fraction f is assumed equal across cells; STK11-LoF cells plausibly have a higher f, which makes every figure below mildly conservative. All four are computable exactly by `build_extract.py --dry-run` without touching an outcome column, and every surviving prereg must report the observed attrition table before locking. Where a cell size IS a real count it is labelled 'real'; where it is derived it is labelled derived and the multipliers are named.

WHAT THE REAL PANEL DISTRIBUTION CHANGES. by_gene_panel is now real: IMPACT468 3919 (50.2%), IMPACT505 2228 (28.5%), IMPACT410 1336 (17.1%), IMPACT341 326 (4.2%). This sizes the MNAR co-mutation problem flagged last time. Restricting to panels covering all required genes costs at most 4.2% if only IMPACT341 lacks coverage, which is tolerable; but the schema publishes no gene-by-panel coverage map, so which panels cover KEAP1, SMARCA4 and STK11 cannot be determined from this file. Each surviving prereg must attach an external panel-coverage manifest to its cohort spec and restrict, not impute. TMB is a separate matter: tmb_nonnull is 7809/7809, so TMB is complete, but completeness is not comparability across four panel footprints, and that is what sinks H-011's dichotomised specification.

CROSS-CUTTING MEASUREMENT NOTES for the survivors. ecog_ps, stage_at_dx, smoking_status, pack_years and metastatic_site are all nlp_extracted with unknown misclassification; no surviving hypothesis uses one as a primary exposure - every surviving exposure is a variant call. days_dx_to_sequencing exists because genomic exposures are ascertained after diagnosis: all three survivors require left-truncated risk-set entry at the sequencing report date, and each prereg must first confirm that days_dx_to_sequencing and treatment.start_day_offset share a common patient origin, since the schema promises only that offsets are relative. treatment.stop_day_offset is a locked-outcome derivative and is used by no surviving analysis. Nothing in this stage reconstructed, or needed to reconstruct, any concept in deliberately_absent.

Next: run 'python3 pipeline/apply_stage.py feasible' then 'python3 pipeline/validate.py feasible_hypotheses'.

missing_fields: PD-L1 tumour proportion score band — still missing as a TPS measure. The schema now carries pdl1_sample_nlp and pdl1_history_nlp, but they are binary NLP-derived positive/negative flags, not percentage bands. H-001 lists PD-L1 only as a covariate, so it survives: the binary flag can be used as a coarse adjustment (pdl1_history_nlp is 79.8% ascertained, 1580/7809 NA; pdl1_sample_nlp is only 42.5% ascertained) and the prereg must state that residual confounding by PD-L1 level remains, on precisely the axis — first-line regimen choice — that this interaction is estimated across. Note that neither pdl1 field is declared in the schema's `tables` section, so a table.field reference for the cohort spec does not yet exist; the schema needs fixing before this term can be written into a spec.

Comorbidity, autoimmune disease, solid-organ transplant and chronic corticosteroid status — the contraindications that now define who receives first-line platinum WITHOUT an ICI. medication_non_oncologic.med_class carries a 'corticosteroid' value, a partial proxy for one of them. Stage 3 named indication bias as the dominant threat to this exact interaction term and the schema cannot fully address it.
Treating site / institution identifier — absent from every table; first_contact_year supplies era but not site.
feasibility.cohort_derivation: The four cells are REAL counts from cohort_counts.by_treatment_exposure, which is NSCLC-specific: ICI/STK11-LoF 336, ICI/STK11-wildtype 2329, platinum-no-ICI-ever/STK11-LoF 163, platinum-no-ICI-ever/STK11-wildtype 1844. Two things must be done to them, both derived. First, the ICI figures are ANY anti-PD-1/PD-L1 exposure in any line, and the hypothesis is first-line: apply A2 (x0.65). Second, both arms lose the EGFR/ALK-activating exclusion (A1) and the stage IIIB-IV/recurrent restriction; combined multiplier x0.85 on the ICI arm and x0.90 on the platinum arm, the latter higher because the platinum-no-ICI-ever definition already selects treated advanced disease. Analysable cells: ICI/mutant 185, ICI/wildtype 1281, chemo/mutant 126, chemo/wildtype 1420. Both the raw-count and the analysable scenarios are carried through the power calculation, because the raw scenario is a hard upper bound and the analysable one depends on A1 and A2. estimated_exposed_n and estimated_comparator_n above report the two STK11-LoF cells; the wildtype cells are the within-arm references. The 163-patient platinum/STK11-LoF cell is the binding constraint and contributes 61% of the interaction variance on its own — the whole design rests on it.
feasibility.minimum_detectable_effect: ratio-of-hazard-ratios 1.55 at f=0.6 on analysable cells (1.44 on raw cells); see power block for the full f-sensitivity

power.estimand: ratio of the STK11 hazard ratio in the first-line ICI arm to the STK11 hazard ratio in the first-line platinum-doublet-without-ICI arm — a treatment-by-STK11 interaction, scale fixed in advance as multiplicative on the hazard. Per R5b this must be pre-registered with --estimand interaction; a within-arm hazard ratio is not this quantity.
power.assumed_event_fraction: f = deaths / analysed patients. Unknown and unknowable at this stage — outcomes are locked and this agent has never seen one. Reported at f = 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8; f = 0.6 is the reference and is a stated assumption, not an observation. A2 (equal f across the four cells) is conservative: the STK11-LoF cells plausibly carry a higher f, which would improve these figures modestly.
power.minimum_detectable_effect: Interaction variance = (1/E_ICImut + 1/E_ICIwt + 1/E_chemomut + 1/E_chemowt), events = cell N x f. RAW REAL CELLS (336/2329/163/1844), sum of inverse patient counts 0.01008: SE(log ROR) = 0.159 / 0.130 / 0.112 at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8, so the smallest detectable ratio-of-hazard-ratios is 1.56 / 1.44 / 1.37. ANALYSABLE CELLS after A1 and A2 (185/1281/126/1420), sum 0.01483: SE = 0.193 / 0.157 / 0.136, minimum detectable ratio 1.72 / 1.55 / 1.46. For comparison the prior formula-derived run reported 1.47 / 1.37 / 1.31 on cells that put ~330 patients in the chemotherapy/mutant cell; the real 163 makes this design measurably weaker.
conditions: THE EQUIVALENCE MARGIN MUST BE 1.5, NOT 1.4. The hypothesis predicts a NULL interaction, so it is an equivalence claim and its power requirement is a margin, not a point alternative. Bounding the ratio-of-hazard-ratios inside 1.4 at 80% power requires SE(log ROR) <= 0.1353 under the two-one-sided-tests convention (one-sided alpha 0.05), which on the analysable cells demands f >= 0.72; under the stricter convention of requiring the whole 95% CI inside the margin it demands f >= 0.91. Neither is a defensible assumption. At the reference f = 0.6 the achievable margins are 1.38 (TOST) and 1.44 (95% CI) on RAW cells and 1.48 (TOST) and 1.55 (95% CI) on ANALYSABLE cells. Prespecify 1.5 under TOST, or 1.6 if the prereg prefers the 95%-CI reading. Do not prespecify 1.4 and do not prespecify 1.25.

Prespecify that a confidence interval which excludes neither 1.0 nor the margin yields an INCONCLUSIVE result, reported as such and sent to the graveyard as inconclusive rather than as a null. The whole value of this hypothesis is that it does not repeat the null-versus-underpowered confusion it was written to correct.

Prespecify the interaction scale before unlock. Stage 3 flagged non-collapsibility: equal biological effects on unequal baseline hazards can produce a non-null hazard-scale interaction. Fix it and do not switch after seeing the estimate (R5).

Report the left-truncation interval distribution (days_dx_to_sequencing minus treatment start) separately BY ARM before the confirmatory run. If the intervals differ materially between the ICI and platinum arms, the truncation biases the interaction term specifically, which is the one quantity this design exists to produce.

Do NOT relax the comparator to 'no ICI in first line' in order to enlarge the 163-patient cell. The platinum-no-ICI-EVER definition is what prevents the comparator contamination stage 3 listed as an alternative explanation; enlarging the cell by relaxing it would trade the design's identification for precision it does not need that badly.
power.adequacy: Adequate, and the best-identified design in the surviving set, but with less headroom than the prior run believed. The predictive interpretation the field asserts implies a ratio-of-hazard-ratios of roughly 1.4 (Skoulidis OS HR ~1.99 on ICI against Shire HR ~1.4 on first-line chemotherapy). The analysable design detects 1.55 at f = 0.6 and 1.46 at f = 0.8 — that is, it can detect the strong form of the predictive claim only if follow-up is mature. Against the equivalence target, bounding the interaction inside 0.67-1.50 would still be a real narrowing of Papillon-Cavanagh's 0.76-1.67 on OS in a cohort roughly six times larger, which is a genuine contribution. What this design CANNOT do is bound the interaction inside 1.25 or exclude a modest ICI-specific effect, and the prereg must say so in advance rather than discovering it afterwards. This is also the only hypothesis in the set with a non-ICI comparator arm, which stage 3 identified as the dominant unresolved axis for the whole file; that value is not reducible to its power.

measurement_concerns: The primary exposure is a variant call (genomic_variant, provenance 'genomic'), the strongest exposure ascertainment available here — not NLP. STK11 loss-of-function is constructible from alteration_type (nonsense / frameshift / splice / deletion) plus oncogenic_annotation for the missense arm, exactly as the hypothesis defines it.

The population filter diagnosis.stage_at_dx is nlp_extracted, so the 'stage IIIB-IV or recurrent' inclusion carries unknown misclassification. by_stage gives Stage 4 = 3421 and Stage 1-3 = 4387 for NSCLC, but a recurrence after an early-stage diagnosis is advanced disease at the time of first-line systemic therapy and is not separable from the stage field alone; is_de_novo_metastatic (derived) and treatment timing partly corroborate.

clinical_annotation_nlp.ecog_ps is nlp_extracted and nullable, and it is the covariate that most directly proxies the indication bias driving arm assignment. Its missingness is likely differential by arm — sicker patients on the non-ICI arm are also the ones whose notes are least complete — so the adjustment is weakest exactly where it is most needed.

MNAR co-mutation via panel_version. The real distribution is IMPACT468 3919, IMPACT505 2228, IMPACT410 1336, IMPACT341 326. The hypothesis requires panels calling STK11, KRAS, KEAP1, TP53 and SMARCA4; the schema publishes no gene-by-panel coverage map, so the restriction must be executed against an external panel manifest attached to the cohort spec. If only IMPACT341 lacks a required gene the cost is 4.2%; if IMPACT410 also lacks one the cost is 21.3%, which would move every figure in the power block. Report the restricted denominator in the prereg before locking.
Left truncation at days_dx_to_sequencing is mandatory. genomic_callable is 7476/7809, so 4.3% of NSCLC patients have no usable genomic ascertainment at all and are excluded, not imputed as wild-type.

treatment.stop_day_offset must not be touched. Time-to-discontinuation is a locked outcome derivative; first-line regimen class is fully determined by drug_class + line_of_therapy + regimen_id + start_day_offset.

missing_fields: PD-L1 TPS band — missing as a band; a binary NLP flag exists (pdl1_history_nlp, 79.8% ascertained). Covariate only here, so not disqualifying: use the binary flag and declare the residual confounding.

Gene-by-panel coverage map — panel_version exists and its distribution is now real (IMPACT468 3919 / IMPACT505 2228 / IMPACT410 1336 / IMPACT341 326), but the schema does not say which panel version calls KEAP1. This matters more for H-002 than for any other hypothesis in the set, because the estimand is a comparison BETWEEN two genes whose panel-adoption histories differ. An external coverage manifest must be attached to the cohort spec and the analysis restricted to panels calling both genes; the restricted denominator must be reported before locking, and if it removes IMPACT410 as well as IMPACT341 the power figures below degrade by ~13%.
feasibility.cohort_derivation: Anchored on real counts, with one prevalence transfer that is stated as an assumption. REAL: NSCLC ICI-treated 2665, of whom 336 STK11-LoF and 2329 STK11-wildtype; KEAP1 any alteration 1034 (13.2% of NSCLC); STK11-and-KEAP1 co-mutant 512, i.e. 50.5% of the 1013 STK11-altered patients also carry KEAP1 — far above the 30% the prior formula-derived run assumed. ASSUMED: KEAP1 prevalence among ICI-treated NSCLC equals the NSCLC-wide 13.2% (likely a slight understatement, since KEAP1 tracks smoking and advanced disease), giving ~353 KEAP1-altered ICI-treated patients; and the 50.5% co-occurrence transfers to the ICI-treated STK11-LoF cell. ICI-treated cells: double-mutant 170, STK11-only 166, KEAP1-only 183, double-wildtype 2146. Restrictions: non-squamous (x0.85, from the real by_histology where LUSC is 822/7809), EGFR/ALK exclusion A1 (x0.85), first-line A2 (x0.65) — combined x0.47. ANALYSABLE: double-mutant 80, STK11-only 78, KEAP1-only 86, double-wildtype 1009. The two identifying single-mutant cells are the two smallest, which is the structural collinearity problem stage 3 flagged, and the real co-occurrence rate makes it worse than the prior run thought.
feasibility.minimum_detectable_effect: gene-versus-gene hazard-ratio ratio 1.76 at f=0.6; KEAP1 main effect 1.35 at f=0.6

power.estimand: difference between the KEAP1-only and the STK11-only log hazard ratios against a common double-wildtype reference. The statement as literally worded — 'the STK11 term attenuates towards the null RELATIVE TO ITS UNADJUSTED ESTIMATE' — is not a testable contrast and must not be pre-registered as one: non-collapsibility of the Cox hazard ratio guarantees some attenuation when any strong prognostic covariate is added, with zero causal contribution from KEAP1. The prereg must adopt the single-mutant contrast as primary.
power.assumed_event_fraction: f unknown; reported at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8, reference 0.6. Note that with a common reference stratum, Var(b_KEAP1 - b_STK11) = 1/E_KEAP1only + 1/E_STK11only — the large reference cell cancels out, so enlarging the double-wildtype group does not help this estimand at all. That is why the cohort's size is misleading here.
power.minimum_detectable_effect: GENE-VERSUS-GENE (primary): sum of inverse patient counts 1/86 + 1/78 = 0.02445; SE = 0.247 / 0.202 / 0.175 at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8, minimum detectable ratio between the two genes' hazard ratios = 2.00 / 1.76 / 1.63. KEAP1 MAIN EFFECT against KEAP1-wildtype with STK11 in the model (166 vs 1087): SE = 0.132 / 0.108 / 0.093, minimum detectable HR = 1.45 / 1.35 / 1.30. STK11-ONLY versus double-wildtype (78 vs 1009): SE = 0.186 / 0.152 / 0.131, minimum detectable HR = 1.68 / 1.53 / 1.45. KEAP1 x STK11 PRODUCT TERM (all four cells, sum 0.03794): SE = 0.251 at f = 0.6, minimum detectable ratio 2.02 — not testable. Prior formula-derived run reported 1.57 for the gene-versus-gene contrast; the real 50.5% co-occurrence rate moves it to 1.76.
conditions: The KEAP1 x STK11 product term the exposure definition proposes ('entered as a separate term with a KEAP1 x STK11 product term') is NOT powered — minimum detectable ratio 2.02 at f = 0.6. It must be prespecified as descriptive, reported with its interval, and explicitly excluded from the FDR-corrected inferential set. Fitting it and interpreting it as a test would be the underpowering this stage exists to catch.

Prespecify that a gene-versus-gene difference smaller than 1.8-fold is INCONCLUSIVE, not evidence that the two genes carry equal signal. The design cannot support an equivalence reading in either direction.

The 'STK11 attenuates relative to unadjusted' limb must be reported as a descriptive coefficient shift with an explicit note that non-collapsibility produces part of it mechanically. It carries no inferential weight.
Label both coefficients as controlled direct effects with the other gene held fixed, not confounder-adjusted total effects. Two co-selected genes conditioned on each other is not ordinary adjustment.

Restrict to panel versions calling BOTH genes and report the restricted denominator before locking. Do not impute KEAP1-wildtype from absence of a call: if KEAP1 entered panels later than STK11, that imputation biases the comparison toward STK11 by exactly the mechanism the hypothesis is trying to adjudicate.
power.adequacy: Marginal but defensible, and weaker than the prior run judged. The published contrasts this hypothesis is scored against are large: the C-CAT cohort reports KEAP1 HR 1.89 with STK11 near null, and De Giglio reports the opposite ordering with STK11 HR 1.97 after adjustment for KEAP1 — both imply a gene-versus-gene ratio near 1.9-2.0, which sits just above the 1.76 detection threshold at f = 0.6. So the design can adjudicate the ordering IF the published effects are real at their published magnitude, and cannot if the true difference is the more likely regressed-to-the-mean 1.4-1.5. The KEAP1 main effect is comfortably powered (1.35) and is the part of this hypothesis worth the most. Passing, but the prereg must carry the 1.8 inconclusiveness bound in writing.

measurement_concerns: Both primary exposures are variant calls, not NLP.

MNAR CO-MUTATION IS ACUTE HERE — more so than for any other survivor — because the estimand is a between-gene comparison and differential callability maps one-to-one onto it. The real panel distribution bounds the cost (4.2% if only IMPACT341 lacks KEAP1, 21.3% if IMPACT410 does too) but the schema cannot tell us which. Restriction, never imputation.

The 50.5% real STK11-KEAP1 co-occurrence is itself the central difficulty: collinearity makes both coefficients unstable and the ordering fragile, and it is far higher than the 30% assumed on the prior schema. The prereg should report the variance inflation factor for the two terms alongside the coefficients.

smoking_status and pack_years are nlp_extracted and are a common cause of both mutations and of survival. They are covariates, not the exposure, but the residual confounding they leave is SHARED between the two coefficients being compared, which partly cancels in the difference — the one place where the NLP weakness is less damaging than usual.

Left truncation at days_dx_to_sequencing required. ICI-only design with no comparator arm, so whichever gene wins is prognostic until a non-ICI arm says otherwise; the schema does contain such an arm (2007 NSCLC platinum-no-ICI-ever patients) if a future version wants it.

missing_fields: PD-L1 TPS band — covariate only; a binary NLP flag exists. Not the reason for rejection.

Cross-tabulation of smoking status with ICI treatment exposure — by_smoking_nlp is now real (Former/Current 5438, Never 2027, Unknown 344) and never_smoker_egfr_alk_wt_stk11lof is a real 34, but neither is crossed with treatment. The share of that 34 who received first-line ICI-containing therapy is derived, not counted, and it is the number the whole hypothesis turns on.
feasibility.cohort_derivation: THE IDENTIFYING CELL IS NOW A REAL COUNT AND IT IS 34, NOT THE 8-10 THE PRIOR RUN ESTIMATED — a fourfold correction in the hypothesis's favour, and it still does not rescue it. The reason: cohort_counts.nsclc_detail.never_smoker_egfr_alk_wt_stk11lof = 34 is a count across ALL 7809 NSCLC patients with no treatment restriction, and this hypothesis is about first-line ICI-containing therapy. The ICI-exposure rate among STK11-LoF patients is a real 46.9% (336/716); applying A2 (65% of those in first line) gives an analysable never-smoker/EGFR-ALK-wildtype/STK11-LoF cell of ~10 patients, or ~16 if the line restriction is dropped. The other three cells: the never-smoker/EGFR-ALK-wildtype denominator can be back-derived from the real 34 — if STK11-LoF prevalence in that stratum matched the NSCLC-wide 9.2% the denominator would be ~370, and since STK11 is tobacco-associated the true prevalence there is lower and the denominator correspondingly larger, so ~370-700 with ~500 taken as the midpoint. That gives never-smoker/STK11-wildtype ~466 raw, ~142 after A1/A2; ever-smoker/STK11-LoF ~208; ever-smoker/STK11-wildtype ~1287. Every one of these except the 34 is derived; the 34 is real and is not the problem.

power.estimand: smoking-by-STK11 interaction on overall survival — the ratio of the STK11 hazard ratio among never-smokers to the STK11 hazard ratio among ever-smokers, within first-line ICI-treated patients.
power.assumed_event_fraction: f unknown; reported at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8. Note that f cannot rescue this hypothesis under any assumption, because f multiplies every cell equally and the binding constraint is the single ~10-patient cell.
power.minimum_detectable_effect: PRIMARY (first-line ICI, cells 10 / 142 / 208 / 1287): sum of inverse patient counts 0.11262, of which the 10-patient cell alone contributes 89%. SE(log ROR) = 0.531 / 0.433 / 0.375 at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8, minimum detectable ratio-of-hazard-ratios = 4.42 / 3.37 / 2.86. ANY-LINE ICI variant (cells 16 / 219 / 320 / 1980): 2.62 at f = 0.6. ABSOLUTE CEILING, dropping the treatment restriction entirely and using the raw 34 against the whole NSCLC cohort (34 / 466 / 682 / 4756): 1.93 at f = 0.6 — and that is a different hypothesis, not this one. Prior formula-derived run reported 'above 3.2' under its realistic scenario and 1.82 under a deliberately generous one; the real counts land at 3.37, i.e. the correction moved the raw cell a long way and moved the answer almost not at all.
power.adequacy: Inadequate by a factor, not a margin. Nothing in the literature or in the mechanism predicts a smoking-by-STK11 interaction of even 1.9-fold, let alone the 2.9-4.4 this design would require. Ricciuti's ever-smoker null implies a modest contrast at most, and the mechanistic argument (lower exposure misclassification in never-smokers, no smoking-driven inflammation to compensate) is an argument for a difference in degree. A cohort that can only detect an implausibly large interaction is inadequate however large the cohort is, and 7809 NSCLC patients do not change that: power here is set by one cell of ten.

measurement_concerns: THE EFFECT MODIFIER THAT DEFINES THE STRATA IS NLP-EXTRACTED. patient.smoking_status has provenance nlp_extracted with a real 'Unknown' bucket of 344 NSCLC patients, and pack_years is nlp_extracted and nullable. Stage 3 already noted that capture is worst at exactly the never/light-former boundary that separates the two strata. Error in an effect modifier attenuates an interaction estimate that is already the weakest quantity in the model, so the nominal figures above are optimistic.

The EGFR/ALK exclusion is what collapses the cell and cannot be relaxed: it removes most never-smokers by design, and reintroducing them reintroduces the driver biology the hypothesis was written to exclude. This is the interaction-in-a-subgroup-of-a-subgroup structure — NSCLC, then first-line ICI, then never-smoker, then EGFR/ALK-wildtype, then STK11-LoF — where power disappears silently.

tmb_mut_per_mb is listed as a covariate while stage 3 placed TMB on the causal path (C-032), so adjusted and unadjusted fits answer different questions. Recorded for completeness; not the reason for rejection.

Differential left truncation: never-smokers are sequenced earlier and more completely because driver testing is standard in that group, so the truncation interval differs systematically between the two strata being compared — a bias that acts directly on the interaction term.
feasibility.reject_reason: Underpowered. The identifying cell is a REAL 34 patients across all NSCLC, a fourfold upward correction on the prior run's estimated 8-10, and the verdict does not move — because 34 is an untreated-restricted count and the hypothesis is about first-line ICI-containing therapy. Only 46.9% of STK11-LoF NSCLC patients received any anti-PD-1/PD-L1 agent (336/716, real) and roughly two thirds of those in first line, leaving ~10 analysable patients in the never-smoker/EGFR-ALK-wildtype/STK11-LoF cell, ~16 if the line restriction is dropped. That cell contributes 89% of the interaction variance on its own. The minimum detectable smoking-by-STK11 ratio-of-hazard-ratios is 3.37 at an assumed 60% event fraction and 2.86 even at 80%; the absolute ceiling, obtained by discarding the treatment restriction entirely and thereby testing a different hypothesis, is 1.93. No published result and no reading of the mechanism predicts an interaction of that size. Compounding it, the modifier defining the strata is nlp_extracted smoking status with misclassification concentrated at the never/ever boundary itself, and the EGFR/ALK exclusion that collapses the cell cannot be relaxed without destroying the contrast. Rejected here rather than carried to pre-registration, where a null would be uninterpretable and a positive result would be noise from single-digit event counts. Recorded in the graveyard with the real cell count, so that the next person who proposes this knows the number is 34 and not a guess.

required_fields: PD-L1 tumour proportion score as a banded percentage (<1% / 1-49% / >=50%) — the stratifying variable that carries the estimand, and an inclusion criterion
PD-L1 assay platform and antibody clone
missing_fields: PD-L1 TPS AS A PERCENTAGE BAND — missing. This was re-examined from scratch because the schema changed: PD-L1 is no longer absent. pdl1_sample_nlp (Yes 2143 / No 1176 / NA 4490) and pdl1_history_nlp (Yes 2988 / No 3241 / NA 1580) are real fields with real counts. They are BINARY positive/negative, derived by NLP from notes. The hypothesis requires three bands, <1%, 1-49% and >=50%, and estimates the KL-versus-KP ordering WITHIN each. A binary 'positive' pools 1-49% with >=50% — precisely the boundary the hypothesis is built on — and a binary 'negative' does not distinguish <1% from a missing or equivocal assay. The two bands that matter cannot be separated, so the load-bearing clause 'and this ordering persists within each PD-L1 expression band' cannot be evaluated.
PD-L1 assay type and antibody clone — absent, and named in the hypothesis's own confounding_risks as a source of non-random misallocation across the 50% threshold.

A table/field reference for the PD-L1 flags — neither pdl1_sample_nlp nor pdl1_history_nlp is declared in the schema's `tables` section; both appear only under cohort_counts.nsclc_detail. There is currently no field name to write into a cohort spec even for the binary version. Flagged as a probable schema bug.

Any sound derivation of TPS — none exists. CD274 amplification is callable from genomic_variant but is a ~1%-prevalence copy-number event and not a protein-expression surrogate. Inferring TPS >= 50% from receipt of ICI monotherapy substitutes a prescribing decision for a measurement and is refused rather than engineered around.
feasibility.cohort_derivation: Carried only far enough to show that power is an independent second objection. REAL: kras_and_stk11lof_comutant = 385 across NSCLC (the KL genotype), and 46.9% of STK11-LoF patients received any anti-PD-1/PD-L1 agent. DERIVED: x0.469 ICI exposure = 181; x0.35 for monotherapy without concurrent platinum (A3) = 63; x0.85 for the EGFR/ALK exclusion and adenocarcinoma restriction = 54; then the hypothesis requires a recorded PD-L1 result, and pdl1_sample_nlp is ascertained for only 42.5% of NSCLC, giving ~23 KL patients with any PD-L1 information at all. Split across three bands that is ~8 per band. Even collapsing to the binary flag the design has ~23 KL patients against a KP comparator of similar order.
feasibility.minimum_detectable_effect: not computable — the stratifying variable does not exist. Indicatively, ~8 KL patients per band would not detect a hazard ratio below roughly 3.

power.estimand: not assessable — the stratification variable the estimand is defined on does not exist in a usable form
power.assumed_event_fraction: not applicable; no power statement is offered for an unconstructible population, because a minimum detectable effect for a stratum that cannot be built is theatre.
power.minimum_detectable_effect: not computable. Indicative only: a within-band KL-versus-KP contrast on ~8 patients per genotype per band would not detect a hazard ratio below roughly 3 at any plausible event fraction, so power is a second and fully independent grounds for rejection even if PD-L1 TPS were added tomorrow.
power.adequacy: not assessable, and independently inadequate on the derived cell sizes

measurement_concerns: Even the binary PD-L1 flag is nlp_extracted, so a version of this hypothesis rebuilt on it would have an NLP-derived PRIMARY stratifier rather than an NLP-derived covariate — materially weaker than a hypothesis whose exposure is a variant call, and it would need to be flagged as such rather than silently accepted.
pdl1_sample_nlp is 57.5% NA (4490/7809). Requiring a PD-L1 result as an inclusion criterion would therefore select on workup completeness, which tracks institution, era and disease burden.

The endpoint concept ('durable clinical benefit', freedom from progression or death beyond a landmark) maps onto 'radiology-assessed progression' and 'best overall response' in deliberately_absent.endpoint_concepts. Naming a locked endpoint concept in a prereg is legitimate and is NOT the objection here; the objection is exposure-side. For the record: no attempt was made or should be made to reconstruct that endpoint from treatment-switch timing in the treatment table, which is explicitly prohibited.

Had TPS existed, the within-band estimate would have been a controlled direct effect and open to collider bias, because STK11 loss lowers PD-L1 through the interferon axis. Stage 3 referred this and it is recorded even though the analysis cannot run.
feasibility.reject_reason: Rejected on a missing required field, and the basis is narrower than at the prior run because the schema changed — so it was re-derived rather than carried over. PD-L1 is no longer absent: pdl1_sample_nlp and pdl1_history_nlp are real NSCLC fields with real counts. But they are binary NLP-derived positive/negative flags, not tumour proportion scores, and the load-bearing clause of the statement is 'this ordering persists within each PD-L1 expression band'. A binary positive pools 1-49% with >=50%, which is exactly the distinction the hypothesis requires; the three bands cannot be constructed and the within-band estimand cannot be defined. Without the stratification the hypothesis degenerates into an unstratified KL-versus-KP comparison, which is the 2018 Skoulidis analysis it exists to supersede and which stage 2 correctly judged confounded by the PD-L1 distribution by construction. Two workarounds are declined rather than engineered around: CD274 amplification is a ~1%-prevalence copy-number event, not a protein-expression proxy; and inferring TPS >= 50% from receipt of ICI monotherapy replaces a measurement with a prescribing decision. Power is an independent second objection — the real KL count is 385 across all NSCLC, of which ~54 survive the monotherapy and driver restrictions and ~23 have any recorded PD-L1 at all, leaving roughly 8 per band. Assay platform and antibody clone, two of the hypothesis's own listed covariates, are also absent. Paired-prereg consequence: H-008 fails on the same field, so the pair stage 3 asked to be pre-registered and interpreted jointly fails symmetrically and neither half is orphaned.

required_fields: PD-L1 tumour proportion score as a percentage, thresholded at >=50% — the population definition, plus the 1-49% and <1% bands for the gradient
PD-L1 assay identity, antibody clone, and the specimen-to-treatment interval
missing_fields: PD-L1 TPS >= 50% AS A POPULATION DEFINITION — missing. The real fields pdl1_sample_nlp and pdl1_history_nlp are binary NLP positive/negative. 'Positive' spans 1-49% and >=50%; the hypothesis IS the >=50% stratum, and additionally predicts a gradient across <1%, 1-49% and >=50%. None of the three bands is constructible, and substituting binary-positive for >=50% would silently redefine the population as roughly PD-L1 >=1%, where the entire premise (an intact interferon axis marked by high PD-L1) does not hold.
PD-L1 assay identity, antibody clone, and the interval between the PD-L1 specimen and treatment start — three of the hypothesis's own listed covariates, none present.
A table/field declaration for the pdl1 flags — they appear only in cohort_counts, not in `tables`.
feasibility.cohort_derivation: Recorded because the power conclusion CHANGED from the prior run and the change matters. REAL: 2665 NSCLC patients received any anti-PD-1/PD-L1 agent, of whom 336 STK11-LoF (12.6%). DERIVED: x0.65 first-line (A2) x0.35 monotherapy (A3) x0.85 EGFR/ALK exclusion (A1) = ~515 first-line ICI-monotherapy patients, ~65 STK11-LoF against ~450 wildtype. Applying the binary PD-L1 restriction that is the closest available approximation to the intended population (ascertained AND positive, ~60% of the monotherapy group) would leave ~39 against ~270. The prior formula-derived run put this at ~121 mutant against ~739 wildtype, roughly double, from a cohort-wide monotherapy figure and a 14.1% prevalence; both were optimistic.
feasibility.minimum_detectable_effect: 1.62 at f=0.6 before any PD-L1 restriction; 1.86 after — against an equivalence claim

power.estimand: STK11 hazard ratio within the PD-L1 TPS >= 50% first-line monotherapy stratum, framed as an EQUIVALENCE claim ('is not associated with shorter overall survival'). An equivalence claim needs tighter precision than a difference claim, not looser.
power.assumed_event_fraction: f unknown; illustrative figures at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8.
power.minimum_detectable_effect: Unrestricted first-line monotherapy (65 vs 450): sum of inverse patient counts 0.01761, SE(log HR) = 0.210 / 0.171 / 0.148 at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8, minimum detectable HR = 1.80 / 1.62 / 1.51, and the 95% interval half-width at f = 0.6 is 0.336, i.e. an equivalence bound of roughly 0.72-1.40 around a null point estimate. With the binary PD-L1 restriction applied (39 vs 270) the bound widens to roughly 0.65-1.54. THIS IS A CHANGE FROM THE PRIOR RUN, which derived SE 0.126 and a bound of 0.78-1.28 and concluded 'power adequate, population unconstructible'. On the real counts the bound of 0.72-1.40 is barely narrower than Papillon-Cavanagh's published 0.76-1.67, and the PD-L1-restricted bound of 0.65-1.54 is not narrower at all. Power now fails too.
power.adequacy: Inadequate on both counts, where the prior run found only one. The population cannot be constructed, AND the equivalence bound the real cohort would support (roughly 0.72-1.40 unrestricted, 0.65-1.54 restricted) does not materially improve on the published intervals this hypothesis was written to tighten. The prior run's more generous conclusion — that the cohort could answer the question if only it recorded PD-L1 — does not survive the real treatment counts.

measurement_concerns: The tempting workaround is refused explicitly. First-line ICI monotherapy is in practice given almost exclusively at TPS >= 50%, so 'received first-line monotherapy' could stand in for the PD-L1 restriction. That substitutes a prescribing decision for a measurement, imports every determinant of regimen choice (age, frailty, disease burden, institution, era) into the stratum definition, makes an unverifiable assumption about the very threshold the hypothesis is about, and destroys the band gradient entirely, since the 1-49% and <1% strata have no monotherapy analogue.

A binary NLP PD-L1 flag would make the population-defining variable nlp_extracted, which for a hypothesis whose entire content is the PD-L1 threshold is a primary-exposure-level weakness, not a covariate-level one.

The hypothesis predicts a null, and exposure misclassification from panel_version-dependent STK11 callability would manufacture exactly that result. An equivalence claim needs its exposure measured better than a difference claim does.

Conditioning on PD-L1 would have been conditioning on a downstream consequence of the exposure, a controlled direct effect open to collider bias. Stage 3 referred this; recorded even though the analysis cannot run.
feasibility.reject_reason: The population is defined by a measurement the dataset does not make, and — a change from the prior assessment — power now fails independently as well. On the field: PD-L1 exists in this schema for the first time, as pdl1_sample_nlp and pdl1_history_nlp, but as binary NLP-derived positive/negative flags. H-008 is not a hypothesis about NSCLC with a PD-L1 covariate; it is a hypothesis about the TPS >= 50% stratum specifically and about the gradient across <1%, 1-49% and >=50%. A binary positive pools 1-49% with >=50%, so substituting it would silently redefine the population as PD-L1 >=1%, where the premise (high PD-L1 marks an intact interferon axis and hence a functionally non-deficient STK11 mutant) simply does not hold. Three of the hypothesis's own covariates — assay, clone, specimen-to-treatment interval — are equally absent, and the pdl1 fields are not even declared in the schema's tables section. On power: the prior formula-derived run concluded the cohort was large enough and died only on measurement. The real treatment counts halve that stratum — 2665 ICI-treated NSCLC patients, 336 STK11-LoF, giving ~65 mutant against ~450 wildtype after the first-line, monotherapy and driver restrictions — and the equivalence bound at an assumed 60% event fraction is roughly 0.72-1.40, against Papillon-Cavanagh's published 0.76-1.67. That is not the advance the hypothesis promised, and applying any PD-L1 restriction widens it to 0.65-1.54, which is no advance at all. Using receipt of first-line monotherapy as a proxy for TPS >= 50% is declined: it replaces a measurement with a prescribing decision and cannot produce the low and intermediate bands the gradient prediction requires. Paired-prereg consequence: H-007 fails on the same field, so stage 3's joint-interpretation instruction lapses cleanly rather than leaving a surviving half to reinterpret.

missing_fields: PD-L1 TPS band — missing as a band; binary NLP flag available. Listed as a covariate, and its absence is arguably a benefit here: stage 3 noted PD-L1 sits downstream of the same interferon axis as the exposure, so adjusting for it would have been mediator adjustment. Drop the term and say so in the prereg; do not substitute the binary flag without declaring the change of estimand.

Gene-by-panel coverage map — panel_version exists with a real distribution, but which versions call STK11 is not stated. KRAS hotspot coverage is near-universal across all four IMPACT panels while STK11 coverage is not, so the four genotype cells are not equally well ascertained and the smallest cell is the most exposed to it. External coverage manifest required on the cohort spec; restricted denominator reported before locking.
feasibility.cohort_derivation: Anchored throughout on real counts. REAL: kras_any_alteration 2195, stk11_loss_of_function 716, kras_and_stk11lof_comutant 385 — so the KRAS-wildtype/STK11-LoF cell, which is the cell every published cohort calls 'null' without being able to distinguish null from underpowered, is a real 716 - 385 = 331 across NSCLC. KRAS-mutant/STK11-LoF-negative = 1810; KRAS-wildtype/STK11-LoF-negative = 5283. REAL ICI-exposure rates, computed from by_treatment_exposure rather than assumed: 46.9% for STK11-LoF (336/716) and 32.8% for STK11-wildtype (2329/7093). Applying those gives ICI-treated cells of 181 / 594 / 155 / 1733 (summing correctly to the real 336 and 2329). DERIVED restrictions: adenocarcinoma (x0.92 on the KRAS-mutant cells, which are LUAD-concentrated; x0.70 on the KRAS-wildtype cells), EGFR/ALK exclusion (x0.99 on KRAS-mutant, x0.72 on KRAS-wildtype, since activating EGFR and ALK events are essentially all KRAS-wildtype), first-line A2 (x0.65 throughout). ANALYSABLE, first-line: KRAS-mut/STK11-LoF 107, KRAS-mut/STK11-wt 352, KRAS-wt/STK11-LoF 51, KRAS-wt/STK11-wt 568. ANY-LINE variant (dividing out A2): 165 / 542 / 78 / 874. The 51-patient KRAS-wildtype/STK11-LoF cell contributes 58% of the interaction variance and is the entire design.
feasibility.minimum_detectable_effect: KRAS-by-STK11 ratio-of-hazard-ratios 1.94 at f=0.6 first-line; 1.71 at f=0.6 any-line

power.estimand: KRAS x STK11 product term on overall survival — the ratio of the STK11 hazard ratio inside the KRAS-mutant stratum to the STK11 hazard ratio outside it. Per R5b this is an interaction and must be pre-registered as one (--estimand interaction --interaction-with KRAS status); two stratified subgroup hazard ratios reported side by side are NOT this quantity and are the error the hypothesis was written to correct.
power.assumed_event_fraction: f unknown; reported at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8, reference 0.6.
power.minimum_detectable_effect: FIRST-LINE (cells 107 / 352 / 51 / 568), sum of inverse patient counts 0.03356: SE(log ROR) = 0.290 / 0.236 / 0.205 at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8, minimum detectable ratio-of-hazard-ratios = 2.25 / 1.94 / 1.78. ANY-LINE with line entered as a covariate (cells 165 / 542 / 78 / 874), sum 0.02187: SE = 0.234 / 0.191 / 0.165, minimum detectable ratio = 1.93 / 1.71 / 1.59. Prior formula-derived run reported 1.70 at f = 0.6 on an 86-patient KRAS-wildtype/STK11-mutant cell; the real first-line-restricted cell is 51 and the figure moves to 1.94.
conditions: THE ANY-LINE SPECIFICATION IS REQUIRED, with line_of_therapy entered as a covariate rather than as a restriction. This is a change to the population as stage 2 wrote it ('first-line ICI-containing therapy') and must be recorded as such in the cohort spec and prereg, not made silently. It is necessary: restricting to first line costs 35% of every cell and moves the minimum detectable interaction from 1.71 to 1.94, which is above most of the range the literature implies. The sensitivity figures above are quoted for the any-line specification; the first-line figures are in the narrative.

Prespecify in advance that a null interaction below a ratio-of-hazard-ratios of 1.7 is INCONCLUSIVE and must not be reported as evidence that the STK11 effect is unconditional on KRAS. Reporting it that way would repeat, at larger scale and with more authority, exactly the null-versus-underpowered confusion this hypothesis exists to resolve — which would be worse than not running it.

Model KEAP1 jointly. KEAP1 co-mutation frequency differs by KRAS status (real: 512 of 1013 STK11-altered patients also carry KEAP1), so an uncontrolled interaction can be carried by KEAP1. This makes H-009 and H-002 share a panel-coverage restriction and they should use the same one.

Record and handle the non-KRAS drivers occupying the KRAS-wildtype cell (MET, BRAF, RET, ERBB2) explicitly. They are callable from genomic_variant.hugo_symbol subject to panel coverage, and their coverage varies by panel_version more than KRAS's does — so the exclusion is executable but its completeness is panel-dependent and must be reported.
Left-truncate risk-set entry at days_dx_to_sequencing and report the truncation-interval distribution by genotype cell.
power.adequacy: Adequate for the upper half of the range the literature implies, and honestly marginal below it. Ricciuti's stratified pattern (STK11 HR roughly 1.6-2.0 among KRAS-mutant against ~1.0 among KRAS-wildtype) implies a ratio-of-hazard-ratios of roughly 1.6-2.0. The any-line design detects 1.71 at f = 0.6 and 1.59 at f = 0.8, so it can resolve the upper part of that range and cannot resolve the lower part; the first-line-restricted design at 1.94 can barely resolve any of it, which is why the any-line specification is made a condition rather than a suggestion. What tips this to a pass rather than an underpowered rejection is that the real KRAS-wildtype/STK11-LoF cell is 331 patients cohort-wide — larger than any published cohort's, and the specific cell whose emptiness makes the existing literature uninterpretable. The design improves on the state of the art even where it cannot settle the question, provided the 1.7 inconclusiveness bound is carried in writing.

measurement_concerns: Both the exposure and the modifier are variant calls — the strongest ascertainment this schema offers, and the reason this hypothesis survives while the NLP-modified ones do not.

MNAR co-mutation is asymmetric here in the worst possible direction: KRAS hotspot coverage is near-universal across IMPACT341/410/468/505 while STK11 coverage is not, so the KRAS-wildtype/STK11-LoF cell — already the smallest at 51 analysable patients — is also the one most likely to be depleted by callability, and 'STK11-wildtype' in the older panels mixes true wildtype with never-tested. Restrict to panels calling both; the real panel distribution bounds the cost at 4.2% (IMPACT341 only) to 21.3% (IMPACT341 + IMPACT410).

smoking_status is nlp_extracted, and KRAS-mutant LUAD is heavily smoking-enriched (real: 5438 ever-smokers against 2027 never-smokers in NSCLC), so stratifying on KRAS is partly stratifying on a variable measured with unknown error. It is a covariate here, not the exposure.
genomic_callable is 7476/7809; the 4.3% without usable genomic ascertainment are excluded, not imputed wild-type.

Left truncation at days_dx_to_sequencing required. ICI-only design, so a positive interaction is prognostic until a non-ICI arm says otherwise — and the schema DOES support such an arm (2007 NSCLC platinum-no-ICI-ever patients, of whom a real 163 are STK11-LoF), which is H-001's design. A future version of H-009 crossed with that arm would be the strongest hypothesis in the file; it is not this one.

required_fields: PD-L1 tumour proportion score, thresholded at >=50% and then modelled continuously within the band — the restriction that makes the regimen contrast interpretable
missing_fields: PD-L1 TPS >= 50% AS A RESTRICTION — missing. The binary NLP flags cannot supply it, and here the substitution is not merely imprecise, it is self-defeating. The hypothesis excludes TPS <50% in its own words 'where monotherapy is rarely used and the comparison would be confounded by indication'. A binary 'positive' includes the 1-49% band, which is exactly the band where monotherapy is rarely used — so restricting to binary-positive readmits the population the restriction exists to remove and reinstates the confounding the design was built to defuse. The design's only stated defence against its own central threat is unavailable.

Treating site / institution — listed as a covariate ('treating site and calendar year of treatment start'). first_contact_year supplies the year; no site or institution identifier exists in any table. Site is a determinant of regimen preference and of how early genotype-aware prescribing was adopted, which is the exposure-dependent-assignment threat.

Comorbidity and frailty measures beyond nlp_extracted ECOG — the dominant determinants of monotherapy versus chemo-immunotherapy choice, and the ones the propensity-score sensitivity analysis the hypothesis proposes would need.
A table/field declaration for the pdl1 flags — present only in cohort_counts, not in `tables`.
feasibility.cohort_derivation: Carried far enough to show that power fails independently. REAL: 336 NSCLC patients are both ICI-exposed and STK11-LoF; 2329 are ICI-exposed and STK11-wildtype. DERIVED: x0.65 first-line (A2) x0.85 non-squamous and EGFR/ALK exclusion = 186 STK11-LoF and 1287 STK11-wildtype on first-line ICI-containing therapy. Splitting by regimen at the assumed 35/65 monotherapy/chemo-immunotherapy ratio (A3) gives STK11-LoF 65 monotherapy and 121 chemo-immunotherapy, STK11-wildtype 450 and 837. The design then requires the TPS >= 50% restriction, which would remove most of the chemo-immunotherapy arm (assume 30% retained, since chemo-immunotherapy is given across all PD-L1 bands while monotherapy is concentrated in the high band): ~36 and ~251. The four interaction cells are therefore roughly 65 / 36 / 450 / 251.

power.estimand: regimen-by-STK11 interaction on overall survival within a restricted PD-L1 band — the ratio of the chemo-immunotherapy-versus-monotherapy hazard ratio in STK11-mutants to the same contrast in STK11-wildtype patients.
power.assumed_event_fraction: f unknown; reported at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8. These figures assume the PD-L1 restriction could be applied, which it cannot; they exist only to show that power is a second, independent objection.
power.minimum_detectable_effect: Cells 65 / 36 / 450 / 251, sum of inverse patient counts 0.04937: SE(log ROR) = 0.351 / 0.287 / 0.248 at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8, minimum detectable ratio-of-hazard-ratios = 2.67 / 2.23 / 2.00. Dropping the PD-L1 restriction enlarges the cells to roughly 65 / 121 / 450 / 837 and improves the figure to ~1.76 at f = 0.6 — but that substitutes an unrestricted comparison of two regimens chosen non-randomly on disease burden and performance status, which is a different and much weaker question, not this hypothesis.
power.adequacy: Inadequate on both counts. No mechanism in the claim graph predicts a regimen-by-STK11 interaction of 2.0-2.7-fold, and the most directly relevant recent evidence points the other way: Skoulidis 2024 argues chemo-immunotherapy is itself compromised in STK11/KEAP1-altered tumours, which would make the true interaction SMALLER than the mechanism predicts, not larger. A design that can only detect an effect the literature argues against is inadequate whatever its total N.

measurement_concerns: The workaround is worse here than for H-007 and H-008 and is refused on stronger grounds: using receipt of monotherapy as a proxy for TPS >= 50% is CIRCULAR, because regimen IS the exposure. The restriction variable and the exposure variable would be the same variable.

Exposure-dependent treatment assignment is the central threat and it is only partly addressable. days_dx_to_sequencing and treatment.start_day_offset do permit modelling whether the STK11 result was available before regimen choice, which is the right handling and is executable — but it cannot repair the missing PD-L1 restriction, and first_contact_year gives era while no site field gives the institution-level adoption gradient.
ecog_ps is nlp_extracted, nullable, and is the only frailty measure the schema offers, while being the dominant determinant of regimen intensity.

treatment.stop_day_offset must not be used to characterise regimen exposure; regimen class is determined by drug_class + regimen_id + start_day_offset within the 28-day window the hypothesis specifies.
feasibility.reject_reason: Rejected on a missing required field, with underpowering as an independent second reason. PD-L1 now exists in this schema as a binary NLP flag, so the rejection was re-derived rather than carried over — and the binary flag makes things worse here rather than better. In H-010 PD-L1 is not a covariate to be dropped; it is the restriction the hypothesis itself introduces to keep confounding by indication from consuming the estimate, and its stated purpose is to exclude TPS <50% 'where monotherapy is rarely used'. A binary 'positive' includes the 1-49% band, which is precisely where monotherapy is rarely used, so substituting it readmits the population the restriction exists to remove and reinstates the confounding it exists to defuse. The obvious alternative — treat receipt of monotherapy as evidence of TPS >= 50% — is circular, because regimen is the exposure being contrasted, and is refused rather than engineered around. Power fails on its own: the real ICI-treated STK11-LoF pool is 336 patients, which after the first-line, non-squamous, driver and regimen splits leaves roughly 65 monotherapy and 121 chemo-immunotherapy STK11-LoF patients, and roughly 36 in the chemo-immunotherapy arm once the required PD-L1 band is applied. The minimum detectable regimen-by-STK11 ratio-of-hazard-ratios is 2.23 at an assumed 60% event fraction, far above anything the mechanism predicts and pointing the opposite way to Skoulidis 2024, which argues chemo-immunotherapy is itself compromised in these tumours. Two further listed covariates, treating site and any comorbidity measure beyond nlp-extracted ECOG, are also absent — and site is exactly the variable the exposure-dependent-prescribing threat requires.

missing_fields: PD-L1 TPS band — binary NLP flag only. Covariate, and one downstream of the same interferon axis as the exposure, so dropping it removes a mediator adjustment rather than a confounder adjustment. Not the reason for rejection.

Panel footprint in megabases and the TMB harmonisation method — panel_version is a categorical label and tmb_mut_per_mb is already per-megabase, but the schema exposes neither the footprint of each IMPACT version nor whether TMB was harmonised across them. The hypothesis's own inclusion criterion, 'TMB reported from a panel with a documented harmonised calculation', therefore cannot be verified from this file. This is not the reason for rejection either, but it forces the choice between a panel-restricted analysis (halving N) and an unverified comparability assumption, and both branches are computed below.
feasibility.cohort_derivation: Anchored on real counts throughout. REAL: 2665 NSCLC patients received any anti-PD-1/PD-L1 agent; of these 336 are STK11-LoF and 2329 STK11-wildtype, so the STK11-LoF fraction among ICI-treated patients is 12.6% — not the 14.1% the prior run assumed from cohort-wide prevalence. REAL: tmb_nonnull = 7809/7809, so TMB is complete and there is no missingness loss, an improvement on the prior run's assumption. REAL: by_gene_panel is IMPACT468 3919 (50.2%), IMPACT505 2228 (28.5%), IMPACT410 1336 (17.1%), IMPACT341 326 (4.2%). DERIVED: x0.85 for the EGFR/ALK exclusion (A1) gives ~2265 analysable patients, ~285 STK11-LoF and ~1980 wildtype. The prior formula-derived run put this at ~3060 analysable with ~430 STK11-mutants, from a cohort-wide 5680 ICI figure and an assumed 70% NSCLC share; the real ICI-treated NSCLC cohort is 2665 and the exposed cell is 22% smaller.
feasibility.minimum_detectable_effect: per-SD ratio-of-hazard-ratios 1.26 at f=0.6 unrestricted; 1.38 panel-restricted; 1.60 dichotomised

power.estimand: TMB x STK11 product term on overall survival — the difference between the TMB slope inside and outside the STK11-LoF stratum, expressed as a ratio of per-standard-deviation hazard ratios for log TMB.
power.assumed_event_fraction: f unknown; reported at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8, reference 0.6.
power.minimum_detectable_effect: CONTINUOUS SPECIFICATION (primary). For a binary exposure X with prevalence p and a standardised continuous modifier Z, Var(beta_interaction) = 1 / (D x p(1-p)) where D is the event count. With p = 0.126 (real) and N = 2265: D = 906 / 1359 / 1812 at f = 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.8, SE = 0.100 / 0.082 / 0.071, minimum detectable per-SD ratio-of-hazard-ratios = 1.32 / 1.26 / 1.22. PANEL-RESTRICTED to IMPACT468 alone (a real 50.2% of NSCLC) for TMB comparability, N = 1137: 1.47 / 1.38 / 1.32. DICHOTOMISED at a TMB-high threshold (q ~ 0.4), residual variance p(1-p)q(1-q) = 0.0264: SE = 0.167 at f = 0.6, minimum detectable ratio 1.60, because the STK11-LoF/TMB-low corner is the sparse one — STK11 mutation itself raises TMB, so the interaction rests on the least populated cell. Prior run reported 1.25 continuous panel-restricted and passed on it; the same calculation on the real cohort gives 1.38 panel-restricted and 1.26 unrestricted.
power.adequacy: Inadequate, and this is the verdict that changed from the prior run. The judgement turns on writing out what effect size the hypothesis actually predicts, which the prior run asserted rather than computed. The estimand is the ratio of the per-SD log-TMB hazard ratio in STK11-mutants to that in STK11-wildtype patients. Within-ICI-arm TMB associations with overall survival in NSCLC are modest: a per-SD hazard ratio of roughly 0.80-0.85 in the wildtype stratum is a fair reading of the published range. The hypothesis predicts the slope is 'attenuated or absent' in STK11-mutants; TOTAL abolition — the strongest form of the claim, HR 1.0 — is then a ratio of only 1.18 to 1.25, which sits BELOW the 1.26 detection threshold at the reference event fraction and below the 1.38 threshold if TMB comparability forces the panel restriction. The design can detect the predicted effect only if the wildtype TMB slope is far steeper than the literature supports (a per-SD HR near 0.73 or below), i.e. only by assuming away the thing that makes the interaction small. This is the four-times-the-events rule biting exactly where the stage brief said it hides: 2265 patients look ample for a main effect and are not ample for an interaction at 12.6% exposure prevalence. The prior run's contrary conclusion rested on an inflated cohort (3060 with 430 mutants against a real 2265 with 285) and on the unexamined assertion that the mechanism implies an effect 'well beyond 1.25-fold'. It does not.

measurement_concerns: Exposure and modifier are both genomic, not NLP — this hypothesis's ascertainment is good and that is not why it dies.

tmb_mut_per_mb is complete (7809/7809, real) but completeness is not comparability. Four panel footprints (IMPACT341/410/468/505, real distribution above) produce TMB estimates that are not interchangeable, and panel choice tracks institution and era while STK11 callability varies with the same panels. Restricting to the dominant panel halves N and moves the detectable effect from 1.26 to 1.38; not restricting requires an unverifiable harmonisation assumption. Neither branch reaches adequacy, which is why the panel question does not need resolving.

Measurement error in an effect modifier attenuates an interaction non-uniformly across strata with different modifier distributions, and STK11-LoF tumours sit higher in the TMB range — so any observed flattening is partly ceiling and curvature rather than modification. A flexible functional form would be needed and would cost further precision.

smoking_status and pack_years are nlp_extracted and are the dominant common cause of both high TMB and STK11 mutation; they are covariates here, not the exposure, but they cannot be measured better in this dataset.

KEAP1 collinearity: KEAP1 also raises TMB and shortens survival, and the real STK11-KEAP1 co-occurrence is 50.5% (512/1013), so joint modelling is required and would consume further degrees of freedom in an already-marginal interaction.

Left truncation at days_dx_to_sequencing required, and the any-line population makes it worse than for the first-line hypotheses because the time origin and the sequencing date can fall in either order.
feasibility.reject_reason: Underpowered for the interaction the hypothesis actually predicts. This verdict CHANGED from the prior stage-4 run, and the change is entirely attributable to the schema going from formula-derived to real. The prior run derived ~3060 analysable ICI-treated NSCLC patients with ~430 STK11-mutants from a cohort-wide ICI count and an assumed NSCLC share; the real figures are 2665 ICI-treated NSCLC patients with 336 STK11-LoF among them, so the exposed cell is 22% smaller and the exposure prevalence is 12.6% rather than 14.1%. On the same continuous specification the minimum detectable per-SD ratio-of-hazard-ratios is 1.26 at an assumed 60% event fraction unrestricted, 1.38 if TMB comparability forces restriction to IMPACT468 (a real 50.2% of the cohort), and 1.60 if TMB is dichotomised. Set against that: the estimand is the ratio of the per-SD TMB hazard ratio in STK11-mutants to that in wildtype patients, and within-ICI-arm TMB slopes in NSCLC correspond to a per-SD hazard ratio of roughly 0.80-0.85, so COMPLETE abolition of the slope in STK11-mutants — the strongest form of the claim — is a ratio of only 1.18-1.25. The design cannot detect it. The prior run passed this on the assertion that the mechanism implies an effect 'well beyond 1.25-fold'; that assertion was never converted into a number, and when it is, it is false for any plausible wildtype slope. This is the interaction-needs-four-times-the-events rule biting where the brief said it hides: 2265 patients is a comfortable main-effect cohort and an inadequate interaction cohort at 12.6% exposure prevalence. The clinical claim the hypothesis exists to support — that TMB-high should not justify ICI monotherapy in an STK11-mutant tumour — is too consequential to rest on an interval that cannot exclude the null under the hypothesis's own best case. Sent to the graveyard rather than to pre-registration, with the note that it becomes viable in a cohort with roughly four times these ICI-treated numbers, or in a pooled multi-institution analysis.

required_fields: Allele-specific or total copy number at the STK11 locus — to distinguish homozygous deletion from shallow heterozygous loss and to convert VAF into a zygosity call
An explicit loss-of-heterozygosity call at the STK11 locus
Cancer cell fraction or clonality estimate per variant
missing_fields: Zygosity / allelic status at STK11 — MISSING, and not soundly derivable from what is present. Nothing in the schema refresh touches this: the new counts are all patient-level aggregates and add no locus-level genomic annotation. The arithmetic showing the derivation is unidentified is in measurement_concerns.

Locus-level copy number — genomic_variant.alteration_type offers only the categorical values 'amplification' and 'deletion', with no copy-number value, no log2 ratio, no allele-specific or minor-allele copy number and no B-allele frequency. The enum treats amplification and deletion as symmetric CNV categories with no depth qualifier, so a 'deletion' call cannot be assumed homozygous — which is exactly what the exposure definition requires.
LOH call — absent. fraction_genome_altered is a genome-wide summary and cannot license a claim about the STK11 locus in an individual tumour.
Clonality / cancer cell fraction — absent. The hypothesis's own alternative_explanations name clonality as a competing operative variable, and it cannot be separated from zygosity without it.
Completeness of tumor_purity — the field is nullable and the schema publishes no completeness figure, so the size of a zygosity-callable subcohort is unknown even under a generous derivation.
PD-L1 TPS band — covariate only, and not the reason for rejection.
feasibility.cohort_derivation: Not the binding constraint, but recorded and now anchored on real counts — and it got worse, not better. REAL: 716 NSCLC patients carry STK11 loss-of-function and 336 of them received any anti-PD-1/PD-L1 agent. DERIVED: x0.65 first-line (A2) x0.85 EGFR/ALK exclusion (A1) = ~186 STK11-LoF patients on first-line ICI-containing therapy, against ~1287 wildtype. The hypothesis splits those 186 three ways — biallelic, monoallelic truncating, monoallelic missense — into cells of roughly 90 / 55 / 40, before any further loss to the low-purity and copy-number-reporting exclusions the population section itself imposes. The prior formula-derived run put this at 90-120 per stratum from a 14.1% cohort-wide prevalence; the real ICI-treated STK11-LoF count of 336 makes the strata smaller.
feasibility.minimum_detectable_effect: ~1.70 between adjacent zygosity strata at f=0.6, and unbounded for the monoallelic-resembles-wildtype equivalence limb

power.estimand: hazard ratio for biallelic versus monoallelic STK11 inactivation, PLUS an equivalence-style claim that monoallelic missense alteration resembles wild-type. The second limb is the more demanding and the less feasible.
power.assumed_event_fraction: f unknown; f = 0.6 used for the illustrative figures, which are secondary to the field objection.
power.minimum_detectable_effect: Biallelic (~93) versus all monoallelic (~93): sum of inverse patient counts 0.02151, SE = 0.189 at f = 0.6, minimum detectable HR between adjacent zygosity strata ~1.70. The equivalence limb is worse and is the one that matters: showing that ~40 monoallelic-missense patients resemble ~1287 wild-type patients would give a 95% equivalence bound wider than 0.60-1.65 at f = 0.6, which excludes nothing the field already believes. Not computed further, because the exposure classification is not identifiable and a power figure for an unmeasurable exposure would be theatre.
power.adequacy: not assessable — the exposure is not identifiable. Secondarily inadequate on cell sizes for the equivalence limb even if it were.

measurement_concerns: WHY VAF + PURITY + ALTERATION_TYPE DOES NOT YIELD ZYGOSITY. The standard inference requires expected VAF = p*m / (p*CN_t + 2(1-p)), where p is tumour purity, CN_t the tumour total copy number at the locus and m the mutant multiplicity. The schema supplies p (nullable) and the observed VAF, and neither CN_t nor m — two unknowns and one observation, so the equation is not identified. Concretely, at p = 0.6 a heterozygous variant in a copy-neutral region gives VAF 0.30, the same variant with LOH (CN 1) gives 0.43, and copy-neutral LOH (CN 2, m 2) gives 0.60 — but a subclonal variant in a gained region can reproduce any of those values, and there is no clonality field to break the tie. The mapping from available fields to exposure strata is many-to-one.

THE COMPARATOR STRATUM IS IN WORSE SHAPE THAN THE EXPOSED ONE. It is defined as 'a single truncating or oncogenic missense variant with RETAINED heterozygosity'. Retained heterozygosity is a positive assertion; the schema supports only the ABSENCE of a deletion call, and absence of a call is not evidence of retention when the panel may not interrogate copy number at that locus at all. The comparator would be constructed from a null result of unknown sensitivity.

MISCLASSIFICATION WOULD BE DIRECTIONAL AND OUTCOME-CORRELATED. Purity-dependent zygosity inference calls low-purity samples monoallelic; purity correlates with tumour content, biopsy site and disease burden, all of which predict survival. The derived exposure contrast would be partly a purity contrast — precisely the artefact the hypothesis's own confounding_risks listed first. Adjusting for tumor_purity does not fix it, because purity would be simultaneously the source of the misclassification and the adjustment covariate.

panel_version-dependent copy-number reporting makes the analysable subcohort non-random with respect to institution and era. The real panel distribution (IMPACT468 50.2%, IMPACT505 28.5%, IMPACT410 17.1%, IMPACT341 4.2%) now sizes this for the first time, but sizing a biased subcohort does not unbias it.
sample_type (primary vs metastasis) is available and would have been the right covariate for specimen-driven purity differences, had the exposure been derivable.
feasibility.reject_reason: The exposure cannot be measured, and nothing in the schema refresh changes that — the new counts are patient-level aggregates and add no locus-level genomic annotation, so this rejection is re-affirmed on re-derivation rather than carried over. Zygosity is genuinely missing rather than nearly present: genomic_variant.alteration_type supplies a bare categorical 'deletion' with no copy-number value, log2 ratio, allele-specific copy number or B-allele frequency, so a deletion call cannot be assumed homozygous; there is no LOH call anywhere; fraction_genome_altered is genome-wide, not locus-level; and there is no clonality or cancer-cell-fraction field. The proposed derivation from VAF and purity is not sound, and the reason is structural rather than a matter of precision: expected VAF = p*m/(p*CN_t + 2(1-p)) contains two unknowns, tumour copy number at the locus and mutant multiplicity, and the schema supplies neither. At 60% purity a heterozygous variant, a variant with LOH and a copy-neutral-LOH variant give VAFs of 0.30, 0.43 and 0.60, and a subclonal variant in a gained region can reproduce any of them. The comparator stratum is worse than the exposed one: 'monoallelic with retained heterozygosity' is a positive assertion that the data can only approximate by the absence of a deletion call, which on a panel that may not interrogate copy number at STK11 is a null result of unknown sensitivity. The resulting misclassification would be directional and outcome-correlated — low-purity samples get called monoallelic, and purity tracks tumour content, biopsy site and disease burden, all prognostic — so the derived contrast would be partly a purity contrast, exactly the artefact the hypothesis itself listed first among its confounding risks, and adjusting for tumor_purity cannot repair it because purity would be both the cause and the adjustment. This is flagged rather than worked around, per the stage rule. Power is secondary and also worse than the prior run believed: the real ICI-treated STK11-LoF pool of 336 gives roughly 90 / 55 / 40 patients across the three zygosity strata after the first-line and driver restrictions, a minimum detectable hazard ratio of ~1.70 between adjacent strata, and an equivalence limb (monoallelic missense resembles wild-type) resting on ~40 patients that could not exclude anything. If this dataset ever carries allele-specific copy number and cancer cell fraction, H-014 is the most mechanistically motivated hypothesis in the set and should be revisited first.
